name: Replacing One Coordinate by a Nonempty Block
statement: For ample $H\subseteq Q_{G\cup\{z\}}$, write $B_i=\rho_z^iH$, $C=B_0\cup B_1$, and $A=B_0\cap B_1$. Replace $z$ by a nonempty block $E$ of size $m$ and set $W_E(H)=(B_0\times\{0_E\})\cup(B_1\times\{1_E\})\cup(C\times(Q_E\setminus\{0_E,1_E\}))$. Then $W_E(H)$ is ample, $|W_E(H)|=(2^m-1)|C|+|A|$, and its shadow is the disjoint union of $\{D\cup T:D\in\operatorname{Sh}(C),T\subsetneq E\}$ and $\{D\cup E:D\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\}$. For nonempty $H$, VC dimension rises by $m-1$. Signed minimal nonfaces avoiding $z$ remain unchanged, and each one containing $z$ replaces it by all of $E$ with the old sign repeated. Dismantlable ampleness, pc-minimal obstruction status for active irredundant input, and cornerlessness are each preserved in both directions. For a forbidden input and $m\ge2$, the output has minimum degree at least three, is its own graph three-core, and has a two-connected crossing graph in which every coordinate of $E$ is universal. The marked construction is uniquely recoverable from its two constant sections or its signed clauses.
proof: The nonconstant block rows all carry $C$, while the two constant rows carry $B_0$ and $B_1$. This gives the displayed shadow and order formulas, and Sandwich equality proves ampleness; minimal nonfaces follow from the same decomposition. A binary replacement lifts each corner deletion of $H$: over an overlap word delete its constant lift, and over an exclusive word delete the two nonconstant lifts before the matching constant lift. Reduction along either new coordinate recovers $H$, proving positivity equivalence; iteration handles all block sizes. Old-coordinate elementary minors commute with replacement, while new-coordinate minors are products or peripheral expansions of the positive proper minors $A,B_i,C$, proving obstruction equivalence. Every new vertex gains at least $m-1$ fibre neighbors, cornerlessness projects through a full fibre, and the shadow formula makes every new coordinate universal. Two universal vertices make the crossing graph two-connected. The two constant sections and clause substitution give unique recovery.
